items.name: Muammar Faiq
items.challenge: Muammar Faiq needed a portfolio for his 2D motion work that converts visitors into clients. It had to stay simple across three main sections without ever looking plain.
items.approach: I kept the layout direct, then used an ASCII hover interaction to give it life. A parallax scroll through the works showcase lets the motion pieces take center stage.

items.name: Beeplus
items.challenge: SlabPixel came with a clear vision: a bold, colorful delivery app website with playful Dribbble energy. The catch was a tight timeline with no room to cut quality.
items.approach: I broke their reference down into typography, colors, and layout to capture what made it feel alive. Four days later, the full landing page was done and fully responsive.

items.name: Mercedes F1
items.challenge: Mercedes AMG F1 had a static website that felt at odds with a team built on speed. The goal was a website that moves, led by the car.
items.approach: I made the car and its parts the key visual across every section. Every hover and scroll sets those parts in motion, so the site moves like the car.

items.name: Sync
items.challenge: Sync needed a product page template they could reuse again and again for every launch. The twist was making sure it never looked like a template or felt basic.
items.approach: I blended the structure of a template with the rhythm of editorial design. Aesthetic imagery and a vibrant gradient give every page enough personality to stand on its own.

items.name: Enso
items.challenge: Enso wanted to leave their glowing, dark mode crypto look behind for something fresh and grounded in traditional finance. It was a full change of direction, not a refresh.
items.approach: I moved the brand onto a light base with a refined typeface and restrained color. Clear structure and generous white space let it read like trusted finance, not crypto.

items.name: Routeonefi
items.challenge: Routeonefi wanted a website that felt illustrative while keeping a clean crypto feel. There were no brand guidelines to lean on, so the whole style started from scratch.
items.approach: I gave every section a simple, semi 3D UI illustration, paired with subtle brand colors and a clean typeface. It has enough character to feel illustrative, never overwhelming.

items.name: Arcania
items.challenge: Arcania is an AI interior design product, so its website had to feel like a designed room. The layout, the type, and every interaction all had to fit.
items.approach: I turned a ruler into the grid, with every section on visible guide lines at the same height. Scrolling through it feels like walking through rooms drawn to scale.

items.name: Onestable
items.challenge: Onestable needed its whole website designed and built in Framer in just four days. Even with that timeline, the result still had to feel polished and never rushed.
items.approach: I used one of my own explorations as the foundation, since the client had already fallen for it. Then I reshaped it around their branding to make it theirs.

items.name: Recruitpilot
items.challenge: Recruitpilot wanted a SaaS look with a glow effect that never pulls attention away from the platform's features. All of it had to be done in just three days.
items.approach: I kept the typography simple and saved the circular glow for the hero and the call to action. Everywhere else, the platform's own interface does the talking.

items.name: Wegonorth
items.challenge: Wegonorth wanted a website that tells their story through a symbol of their own. That symbol had to carry the company motto at its heart, which is moving forward.
items.approach: I chose a compass as the key visual and let its movement run through the website. Every scroll animation and every hover follows it, always pointing the way forward.

items.name: Anywear
items.challenge: Anywear needed one landing page for their mobile app that unites three different worlds. SaaS, mobile app, and an editorial layout all had to read as a single concept.
items.approach: I built the layout on editorial principles with generous white space, giving the fashion room to breathe. UI elements bring in the tech side and show off the app.

items.name: Lexur
items.challenge: Lexur wanted the dark, glowing crypto look without it ever feeling overwhelming. Glow and simplicity had to stay in balance, with only two days to make it happen.
items.approach: I used simple illustrations for the core sections and saved the vibrant glow for the hero and the call to action. A simple typeface keeps everything else clean.

items.name: Webser
items.challenge: Webser wanted an editorial website for their agency, with straightforward content and a clear structure. The hard part was keeping it simple without it looking plain or templated.
items.approach: I took a semi editorial direction and chose solid colors over gradients. Then I created retro artwork from their branding, giving the visuals a character of their own.
